stem: Meena chews a piece of plain boiled rice slowly for two minutes and it begins to taste sweet. When she tests the chewed rice with iodine solution, there is little or no blue-black colour. What do these observations show?

options.text: Iodine removes the starch from the chewed rice.
Saliva in the mouth changes some of the starch into sugar.
Boiled rice is naturally sweet, so chewing has no effect.
Chewing turns the sugar in the rice into starch.

teacher.key_rationale: Chewing mixes rice with saliva, whose enzyme breaks starch into sugar; this explains both the sweet taste and the weak iodine result. A reverses the role of iodine, C denies the action of saliva, and D reverses the starch-to-sugar direction. Key B recalculated.
